{"results":[{"doc_id":"kb-loan-products","title":"Kaveri Bank (fictional): loan products and interest rates","date":"2026-11-01","section":"Home loans: a floating rate linked to the repo rate","passage":"Home loans: a floating rate linked to the repo rate
Kaveri Bank's home loans have a floating rate linked to the RBI policy repo rate, through its External Benchmark Lending Rate (EBLR).

- EBLR = the RBI policy repo rate + 2.65 percentage points.
- Home loan rate = EBLR + a spread set by the CIBIL score at approval: 750 and above, no spread (+0.00); 700 to 749, +0.45 percentage point; below 700, +1.05 percentage points.
- The rate resets on the first day of the month after a change in the repo rate. The spread stays the same for the life of the loan.

Kaveri Bank charges nothing to prepay part of a floating-rate home loan, or to close it in full, at any time and from any source of funds."},{"doc_id":"kb-faq","title":"Kaveri Bank (fictional): product questions and answers","date":"2026-11-01","section":"Can I prepay my home loan without a charge?","passage":"Can I prepay my home loan without a charge?
Yes, if it is on a floating rate: Kaveri Bank charges nothing to prepay or close a floating-rate home loan. Personal, two-wheeler and car loans have their own rules (see the prepayment and foreclosure rules)."}]}

Set by the RBI's Monetary Policy Committee at its meeting of 5 to 7 October 2026 (announced 7 October 2026), and still in force on 6 November 2026:

- Policy repo rate: 5.50%, raised from 5.25%.
- Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) rate: 5.25%.
- Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) rate and Bank Rate: 5.75%.

The next meeting of the Monetary Policy Committee is scheduled for 2 to 4 December 2026.
